subject: Re: Load test coordination and SLO requirements - FinWise
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@finwise.com>, Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finwise.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + load test next steps

Hi Samantha / Alex — great to meet earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side so we can align on the customer-led load test: 

Recap of SLO/targets you mentioned:
- Streaming P95 latency target: <= 350 ms (end-to-end for typical prompt sizes)
- Concurrency target: 150 concurrent user sessions (with occasional spikes to 250)
- Throughput: target steady-state ~500 requests/sec; peak bursts up to 750 req/sec for short windows
- Streaming support required (chunked responses, ~20-60 token chunks)

What we need from FinWise to run your customer-led test:
1) Preferred test harness: you said k6 (good) — please confirm k6 script deliverable or we can provide a starter script.
2) Test accounts: service account API key + example user session tokens (we can provide a secure upload link)
3) IP allowlist: we need the public IP ranges for your test runners so we can add them to the allowlist and firewall rules
4) Test window: propose 2027-03-17 02:00–06:00 UTC (Redwood team can provide on-call support) — please confirm if this works for your ops window
5) Warmup and ramp strategy: recommend 15–20m warmup, 30m steady-state, then 10–15m ramp-down.

Action items / next steps:
- Samantha: confirm test window + send IP ranges and preferred k6 script (or let us know if you want our starter script).
- Redwood (Marissa/Rishi): prep environment (streaming endpoints enabled, dedicated worker group if needed), set up test account, add allowlist when IPs provided, and monitor metrics.

I’ve copied Marissa and Rishi to coordinate the infra side. I attached a starter k6 script and a runbook stub for visibility.

Thanks —
Logan Wright
Enterprise AE
Redwood Inference
(415) 555-0124
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@finwise.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finwise.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + load test next steps

Thanks Logan — that recap looks right. A few clarifications and confirmations from FinWise: 

1) We prefer k6. I attached our internal k6 runner (we'll send the final test scripts by Monday) — if you have any adjustments to make for streaming requests let us know.
2) Target confirmation: P95 <=350ms for streaming (we want to be conservative), concurrency 150 steady, allow bursts to 250 for up to 5 minutes.
3) Test window: 2027-03-17 02:00–06:00 UTC works for us.
4) IPs for allowlist (attached in finwise-ip-allowlist.csv) — these are the public NATs for our k6 runners.
5) Test accounts: we will share a scoped API key (test only). We'll either upload to your secure share or paste into the secure link you provide.

A couple of asks for Redwood during the run:
- Please enable detailed per-request tracing for the test window (request ID passthrough) so we can correlate latencies.
- Keep streaming chunk sizes intact (we'll validate chunk boundaries) — if there are any timeouts or premature closes please signal immediately on the escalation channel.

I'll attach the CSV with IPs and plan to send the scripts Monday. Thanks for looping in your SRE folks.

Best,
Samantha Lee
Head of Platform
FinWise
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>

Subject: Fwd: Post-call recap + load test next steps (FinWise)

Marissa / Rishi — forwarding FinWise confirmation. Key asks: enable tracing during the window, prepare streaming endpoint, add IPs from their CSV to allowlist, create scoped test account. They plan to run k6 and will send scripts Monday.

Can you confirm:
- rough capacity needed (GPUs / worker groups) to sustain 500 rps / 250 concurrency bursts,
- monitoring hooks we should enable (span-level tracing, per-route token-level latency), and
- owner for on-call escalation during the run?

I attached the k6 starter script we discussed (finwise-k6-script.js).

Thanks —
Logan
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-call recap + load test next steps (FinWise)

Putting a short runbook together and will lead the run. Preliminary notes: 

Capacity planning:
- For 500 rps with streaming responses and 250 concurrency spikes, recommend provisioning a dedicated worker group with 4x A100-equivalent GPUs (or equivalent runtime capacity). We can scale pods horizontally with max concurrency per pod set to 50. That gives headroom for bursts.
- Enable autoscaling with a 60s decision window and a burst policy to let pods oversubscribe briefly during the first 5 minutes of a spike.

Monitoring / tracing:
- Enable request-level tracing (X-Request-ID passthrough) and increase tracing sampling to 25% for the test window.
- Add k6 metrics ingestion into our per-route dashboards (latency p50/p95/p99, error rates, token throughput).

Operational steps:
1) Rishi to create scoped test account + upload creds to secure share (I will not accept creds over email).
2) Add FinWise IP ranges to the allowlist (rishi to confirm when applied).
3) Toggle streaming-specific timeouts to 120s for the test window to avoid premature closes.
4) Warmup: 20m gradual ramp to 150 concurrency, then hold to steady-state.

Attachments: runbook draft and suggested k6 config (I used Logan's starter and added streaming helpers). I'll circulate the runbook in Drive and link in the ticket.

I can be the on-call owner during the window; Logan, please confirm we have an escalation channel with FinWise (Slack / PagerDuty).

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Reliability Solutions
Redwood Inference
